correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the operator boundary conditions and the full ground-state quantifiers. Positivity and simplicity make the two-site reflection symmetry effective; each arc is solved explicitly, positivity fixes the branch, the delta jump gives a strictly increasing scalar secular equation, and strict convexity of tan compares every asymmetric root with the antipodal root. The transfer-matrix verifier independently checks the scalar secular equation at representative weak, intermediate, and strong couplings. No finite experiment is used to infer the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2019 paper proves the repulsive loop optimizer only for weak and sufficiently strong coupling and explicitly leaves all positive coupling as Conjecture 5.1. The new theorem resolves the complete N=2 case by a reduction not stated there. Searches for the conjecture, two-delta periodic-loop secular equations, antipodal/equidistant optimization, and later resolutions found no published equivalent or stronger all-coupling N=2 theorem.

value.rationale: The result settles the first nontrivial all-coupling case of an explicit published spectral-optimization conjecture, including precisely the intermediate regime left between perturbative and strong-coupling arguments. It gives an exact one-variable secular law and identifies the structural reason N=2 is tractable. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or a numerical recomputation.
